If SIB1 is not transmitted, it is still possible to configure a UE with ControlResourceSetZero and searchSpaceZero via dedicated signalling, as there is no requirement for this configuration to be consistent with the one in pdcch-ConfigSIB1 (which does not indicate CORESET#0 and searchspace#0 if SIB1 is not transmitted). 
However this is not clear in the specification.
properties.summaryOfChange:
In PDCCH-ConfigCommon and in ServingCellConfigCommon it is clarified that ControlResourceSetZero and searchSpaceZero can be configured even if SIB1 is not transmitted.
Impact analysis
Impacted functionality: PSCell and SCell configuration in EN-DC
Inter-operability: 
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE may release the configuration for ControlResourceSetZero and searchSpaceZero when acquiring MIB.
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there are no inter-operability problems.

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The UE behaviour will remain unspecified if a UE  in the RRC_INACTIVE state will leaving "camped normally" mode.
properties.reasonForChange:
During the RAN2#103bis meeting, RAN WG2 confirmed the working assumption that a UE in RRC_INACTIVE shall stay in this state upon leaving "camped normally” mode (unit another suitable is found).

Following further feedback from CT WG1, it is also clarified that if a UE fails to find a suitable cell and resorts for camping on the acceptable cell, then the UE moves to RRC_IDLE.
properties.summaryOfChange:
In 5.2.2, UE state diagram is extended so that a UE moves to RRC_IDLE only if it fails to find a suitable cell.
In 5.2.7, it is clarified that a UE shall first search for the suitable cell. Only if it fails, then a UE tries to camp on the acceptable cell.

Impact analysis
Impacted functionality:
RRC_INACTIVE state
Inter-operability: 
If a UE is not implemented according to the CR but the network is not, then a UE might go to the RRC_IDLE state more often than the network anticipates.
If a UE is implemented according to the CR but the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue.

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: Procedure text does not cover the Inter RAT cell reselection cases while the UE is in RRC_INACTIVE state.
properties.reasonForChange:
In Release 15, mobility to other RAT in RRC_INACTIVE is not supported. For cell reselection while in RRC_INACTIVE it is however still possible that UE reselects to other RAT. Then, the UE should transition to RRC_IDLE (and start RRC setup in new RAT). 
This should be reflected in 38.331.
A new section needs to be added in resume section to describe that at Inter-RAT reselection, the UE should go to IDLE. The reason for introducing a new section is that there is no other section in Inactive state that covers reseletion aspects.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Add procedure text for reselecting an Inter-RAT in 5.3.13.X

Impact analysis:
There is no network implementation related to this change
If the UE does not implement this change, it may remain in wrong state and store invalid context, e.g., after having changed RAT.

properties.title: Configuration of SCG during RRC Resume in NGEN-DC (36.331)

properties.content:
The configured SCells (MCG and SCG) can be configured in deactivated or activated state by RRC upon addition or after a handover.  Timing requirements are up to RAN4.  FFS if this applies to resume.
R2-1900695	Configuring or resuming SCG in RRCResume for NR-DC and NE-DC	Ericsson	discussion	Rel-16	LTE_NR_DC_CA_enh-Core
=>	Not treated
R2-1900697	Configuring or resuming SCG in RRCConnectionResume for (NG)EN-DC	Ericsson	discussion	Rel-16	LTE_NR_DC_CA_enh-Core
=>	Not treated
R2-1900698	Configuration of SCG during RRC Resume in NGEN-DC (36.331)	Ericsson	draftCR	Rel-16	36.331	15.4.0	B	LTE_NR_DC_CA_enh-Core
Proposal 1	Enable configuration of NR SCG in for (NG)EN-DC in RRCConnectionResume
Proposal 2	Enable delta signalling of NR SCG for (NG)EN-DC in RRCConnectionResume
-	Intel explains that the UE keeps in the configuration memory but doesn’t apply it.  CATT thinks this is the only way to do it and indicates that it doesn’t imply autonomous UE actions.  Oppo agrees to be supported
-	Nokia asks if this improving latency or just signalling.  Ericsson explains that we are saving one round trip time as otherwise we have to wait for RRC reconfiguration.
-	Huawei agrees that there is a benefit to save time but the delta signalling is not a small optimization and there may be other ways.
-	Nokia thinks that we first have to determine when the early measurements are available.
-	CATT doesn’t understand why we don’t allow the blind configuration.  Interdigital also agrees and we did something similar to NR Scells.
-	LG has some concerns on the blind addition
-	Mediatek questions the benefits especially if the SCell is not the right one.  Qualcomm thinks that we should consider this case.
-	Ericsson thinks that there are some deployments where it may make sense for the network and we shouldn’t put limitations.  Nokia thinks that there may be some impacts to RAN4 and it is not only us that are impacted here.
-	Apple ask if the network can give the RRCresume and RRCreconfiguration at the same time.  Interdigital thinks that it may be possible for re-establishment but not for resume.
=>	Noted

properties.title: Correction on RRC processing delay

properties.content:
1	For TS 38.331, RRC processing delay for UE capability transfer is [15-80] ms.
2	For TS 36.331, RRC processing delay for UE capability transfer to report NR band combinations and/or MR-DC band combinations is corrected to [15-80] ms.
3 	Not define RRC processing delay for the combined procedure of SecurityModeCommand and RRCConnectionReconfiguration.
4	RRC processing delay for RRCReestablishment is 10 ms
5 	Not define RRC processing delay for the combined procedure of RRCReestablishment and RRCConnectionReconfiguration.
=>	Offline discussion to progress the UE capability transfer number (Offline discussion 87, Qualcomm)
R2-1901308	RRC UE processing time for RRCResume	Ericsson	discussion	Rel-15	NR_newRAT-Core	R2-1817524
-	MediaTek clarify that in LTE the reduced processing delay is optional with capability. Also think the 3ms delay is not feasible from UE point of view and think it is not necessary to decide on a reduced delay at this time.
-	Huawei think we have already sent IMT2020 performance results based on what was possible in LTE. So NR should be able to meet this performance. Open for it to be optional as it was in LTE.
-	Intel think even with 10ms requirement the IMT 2020 delay requirement can be met. Qualcomm support the Intel view.
-	Ericsson shares the view of Huawei and by lowering the delay we can meet the 3GPP requirement of 10ms.
-	ZTE think it would be good to have the same value as possible in LTE.
-	Intel think the LTE discussion was a very simplified configuration that was not very useable in practice, just to meet the IMT2020 requirement. For NR we can meet the IMT2020 requirement anyway so we don’t need to follow the LTE approach.
-	Samsung think the self-evaluation can be changed.
=>	Comeback Friday to confirm whether the LTE approach  of defining a capability for this reduced processing performance for a Resume procedure with the same configuration limitations as LTE can be agreed. See 37.910 table 5.7.2.1-1 for NR performance in IMT submission (Offline discussion 88, Huawei)
-	Update from offline: The proposal is to try to agree an approach that copies the LTE solution for meeting the IMT2020 requirements including a capability.
=>	Agree to follow the LTE approach  of defining a capability for this reduced processing performance for a Resume procedure with the same configuration limitations as LTE can be agreed

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved:
The UE is required to filter the featureSetsDownlinkPerCC or featureSetsUplinkPerCC entries in featureSets such that the reported bandwidth in these entries are always not higher the NW requested maxBandwidthRequestedDL, maxBandwidthRequestedUL. The UE may have to create additional entries of featureSetsDownlinkPerCC or featureSetsUplinkPerCC and corresponding featureSetsDownlink or featureSetsUplink for this requirement, which can increase the UE capability size unnecessarily. 

The number of FeatureSetDownlinkPerCC-Ids the UE is allowed to report in featureSetListPerDownlinkCC is restricted to the number of carriers according to the ca-bandwidthClassDL of the band combination that refers this featureSetListPerDownlinkCC.. 

Similarly, the number of FeatureSetUplinkPerCC-Ids the UE is allowed to report in featureSetListPerUplinkCC is restricted to the number of carriers according to the ca-bandwidthClassUL of the band combination that refers this featureSetListPerUplinkCC.. 
 
Impact Analysis:
Impacted 5G architecture options: 
Standalone, EN-DC
Impacted functionality: 
FeatureSets Capability signalling 
Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operabiilty issue, as the UE limits to reporting only the bandwidths and number of carriers that do not exceed what the NW requested.

If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, if the network does not expect the UE to report featureSet parameters that exceed the maxBandwidthRequestedDL, maxBandwidthRequestedUL, maxCarriersRequestedDL,or maxCarriersRequestedUL, whichever are provided by the network or if the network does not expect the UE to report featureSet parameters that exceed number of FeatureSetDownlinkPerCC-Ids the UE is allowed to report,  then the NW behaviour is unknown. Otherwise there is no interoperability.
properties.reasonForChange:
In the current procedure of compiling the UE capability information for provided NW filters, 38.331 states that the IE featureSets should exclude entries for fallback band combinations with same or lower capabilities and where the parameters do not exceed maxBandwidthRequestedDL, maxBandwidthRequestedUL, maxCarriersRequestedDL or maxCarriersRequestedUL, whichever are received.

But in RAN2- NR AdHoc 1807, an agreement was made and an LS was sent to RAN1 (R2-1810975) stating that UEs are assumed to support as fallback capabilities, the bandwidth, MIMO layers and MCS of a lower value than what is reported in featureSetsDownlinkPerCC or featureSetsUplinkPerCC. The additional condition for bandwidth is that the UE is expected to support only the lower bandwidths that are supported using IEs channelBWs-DL-v1530  and channelBWs-UL-v1530  for a particular band. In addition, 38.306 captures the description of bandwidth (DL/UL) fields from featureSet(DL/UL)PerCC as “Indicates maximum DL(/UL) channel bandwidth supported for a given SCS that UE supports within a single CC…..”. This reflects that the UE can provide the maximum BW and the lower BWs are supported and so there is no need for the UE to restrict the reported bandwidth to maxBandwidthRequestedDL, maxBandwidthRequestedUL, if the UE supports higher BW.


It was also agreed in RAN2, that the UE is allowed to use an entry in featureSet, where the number of CCs pointed to by featureSetDownlink can have more featureSetDownlinkPerCC entries than the band combination that is using this featureSetCombination allows. This applied to uplink as well where  featureSetUplink can have more featureSetDownlinkPerCC than what the featureSetCombination allows. The NW can choose from the set of featureSetDownlinkPerCC or featureSetUpPerCC entries in such a case. 

But the below 38.331 reference does not clearly captures this:

featureSetListPerDownlinkCC
Indicates which features the UE supports on the individual carriers of the feature set (and hence of a band entry that refer to the feature set). The UE shall hence include as many FeatureSetDownlinkPerCC-Id in this list as the number of carriers it supports according to the ca-bandwidthClassDL. The order of the elements in this list is not relevant, i.e., the network may configure any of the carriers in accordance with any of the FeatureSetDownlinkPerCC-Id in this list.

It is not necessary for the UE to restrict providing only the featureSets with entries that do not exceed the NW requested bandwidth, or to restrict the number of CCs in the cases where it can support more. 

The restriction is already made on the ‘candidate band combinations’ and featureSets do not have to be restricted. They can be re-used by other band combinations as well.

Otherwise the UE would have to create additional featureSetsDownlinkPerCC or featureSetsUplinkPerCC and possibly the corresponding featureSetsDownlinkPerCC or featureSetsUplinkPerCC which results in an increase in capability size.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Add the text in the procedural text that gives the UE the option to restrict featureSets to limit to the NW requested parameters. 

Clarify the field description in featureSetListPerDownlinkCC and featureSetListPerUplinkCC to accurately reflect the RAN2 agreement.

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: NR specifications would be not consistent with TR 37.910 and LTE CR in R2-1813109 regards to the ITU-2020 requirement on control plane latency for the processing of RRCConnectionResume message.
properties.reasonForChange: To meet the ITU-2020 requirements on control plane latency in NR consistently with TR 37.910 and LTE CR in R2-1813109, the processing delay requirements when the UE receives RRCConnectionResume is reduced.
properties.summaryOfChange:
The processing delay requirement for RRC connection establisment for the case when the UE receives RRCConnectionResume is reduced in case the UE supports it.
An optional capability bit is added for this feature.

Impact analysis:
Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone
Impacted functionality:
The CR only impacts the processing delay requirements for RRC Resume procedure.
Inter-operability:
There is no inter-operability problem caused by this CR.
properties.title: CR on Processing delay requirements for RRC Resume procedures in TS 38.306

properties.content:
1	For TS 38.331, RRC processing delay for UE capability transfer is [15-80] ms.
2	For TS 36.331, RRC processing delay for UE capability transfer to report NR band combinations and/or MR-DC band combinations is corrected to [15-80] ms.
3 	Not define RRC processing delay for the combined procedure of SecurityModeCommand and RRCConnectionReconfiguration.
4	RRC processing delay for RRCReestablishment is 10 ms
5 	Not define RRC processing delay for the combined procedure of RRCReestablishment and RRCConnectionReconfiguration.
=>	Offline discussion to progress the UE capability transfer number (Offline discussion 87, Qualcomm)
R2-1901308	RRC UE processing time for RRCResume	Ericsson	discussion	Rel-15	NR_newRAT-Core	R2-1817524
-	MediaTek clarify that in LTE the reduced processing delay is optional with capability. Also think the 3ms delay is not feasible from UE point of view and think it is not necessary to decide on a reduced delay at this time.
-	Huawei think we have already sent IMT2020 performance results based on what was possible in LTE. So NR should be able to meet this performance. Open for it to be optional as it was in LTE.
-	Intel think even with 10ms requirement the IMT 2020 delay requirement can be met. Qualcomm support the Intel view.
-	Ericsson shares the view of Huawei and by lowering the delay we can meet the 3GPP requirement of 10ms.
-	ZTE think it would be good to have the same value as possible in LTE.
-	Intel think the LTE discussion was a very simplified configuration that was not very useable in practice, just to meet the IMT2020 requirement. For NR we can meet the IMT2020 requirement anyway so we don’t need to follow the LTE approach.
-	Samsung think the self-evaluation can be changed.
=>	Comeback Friday to confirm whether the LTE approach  of defining a capability for this reduced processing performance for a Resume procedure with the same configuration limitations as LTE can be agreed. See 37.910 table 5.7.2.1-1 for NR performance in IMT submission (Offline discussion 88, Huawei)
-	Update from offline: The proposal is to try to agree an approach that copies the LTE solution for meeting the IMT2020 requirements including a capability.
=>	Agree to follow the LTE approach  of defining a capability for this reduced processing performance for a Resume procedure with the same configuration limitations as LTE can be agreed

The CR adresses the following issues
 Name of secondary RLC bearer mistakenly suggest that duplication is used when configured
 For SRBs configred with LTE PDCP it is not clear that PDCP that duplication is activated when a secondary RLC bearer is configured (no PDCP config)
 It is not clear in which cases network can configure an RLC bearer for SRBs

properties.summaryOfChange:
The CR includes the following changes

 General clarifications
For secondary RLC bearer field and IE name is changed to rlc-BearerConfigSecondary
Clarify that for SRBs configured with LTE PDCP, that when 2 RLC entities/ bearers are configured that: a) duplication is always activated and that b) value infinity applies for t-Reordering. This is clarified in the procedural specifications (i.e. upon addition of 2nd RLC entity)
 Introduce some clarifications regarding the signalling
For SRBs, a secondary RLC bearer is only configured for MCG
 Clarify the UE behavior upon release of an LTE RLC entity as follows
No action upon release of a secondary RLC entity in a cell group/ MCG
Specify that UE performs RLC re-establishment upon release of (primary) RLC enity in other cell group (split to MCG or to SCG)

Changes in update
Updated in accordance with R2-1902702 e.g. addition of aspects also relevant for HRLLC like additon of RLC extension for SRBs, removal of NE-DC specific aspects (i.e. in late drop CR only): 5.3.10.2 

Changes in revision 2
Removed within SRB-ToAddMod the addition of rlc-Config-v15x0 (reestablishRLC-r15) i.e. in LTE DC SCG RLC bearer of all RBs is re-established upon security refresh due to use of HO
In 5.3.10.17 there was a minor wording change regarding the check whether the SRB has an LTE PDCP entity (as field pdcp-Config is not used for SRBs)
Upon DRB type change between MCG and SCG DRB, both the primary and secondary RLC entities/ logical channels are ported from MCG to SCG configuration (or vice versa)

properties.abstract: => Results of Email [105#20][NR] intra-NR handover related capabilities CR to 38.306 (ZTE).
properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: It is unclear those capabilites are applicable to only NR SA, or only EN-DC, or both. Which results in misinterpretation between network and UE.
properties.reasonForChange:
Currently, the intra-NR handover and measurement related capabilites(e.g. handoverFDD-TDD, handoverFR1-FR2, handoverInterF, intraAndInterF-MeasAndReport, eventA-MeasAndReport) are only defined in UE-NR-Capability. However, it is unclear whether these capabilites are applicable to NR SA(e.g. PCell handover) or EN-DC(e.g. PSCell change).
During RAN2_105meeting, following agreements are made:
This CR is provided to capture above agreements.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Add “This field only applies to NR SA (e.g. PCell handover). For PSCell change when EN-DC is configured, this feature is mandatory supported.” to the field description of handoverFDD-TDD, handoverFR1-FR2 and handoverInterF.
Add “This field only applies to SN configured measurement when EN-DC is configured. For NR SA, this feature is mandatory supported.” to the field description of intraAndInterF-MeasAndReport and eventA-MeasAndReport. 

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options:
NR SA, EN-DC

Impacted functionality:
PCell measurement and handover in NR SA;
SN configured measurement and PSCell change in EN-DC

Inter-operability: 

For change1: 
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, network assumes UE does not support the related PSCell change type based on current bits, and cannot trigger trigger PSCell change accordingly.
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE is impossible to signal the different capabilities for PCell handover and PSCell change, which will cause misunderstanding between network and UE.

For change2: 
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, if network assumes the current bits are applicable to NR SA, while UE does not support this features for SN configured measurement. Then for NR SA UEs, network is unable to configure the measurement to UE, which cannot trigger PCell handover accordingly. 
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE is impossible to signal the different capabilities for NR SA measurement and SN configured measurement, which will cause misunderstanding between network and UE.

-	Ericsson think that it is clear in 38.331 that the UE moves to idle when it changes RAT.

properties.title: dCR 38331 RRC Segmentation - UL

properties.content:
1	The segmentation mechanism should be defined in ASN.1 in a generic manner so that it could in principle be applied in future to any uplink and downlink RRC message.
2	RAN2 will decides explicitly which RRC messages may be segmented.
2a	Within this WI, segmentation of UE capability information message will be specified.
3	A transmitter (UE or NW) may only use segmentation if it knows that the receiver (NR or UE) comprehends it.
3a	The network indicates in the UECapabilityEnquiry message whether the UE may apply RRC segmentation to its UECapabilityInformation
4	The transmitting entity (UE or NW) uses segmentation only if the unsegmented message exceeds the size limit of PDCP

properties.title: Introduction of early RLF declaration or fast handover failure recovery for PSCell in MR-DC

properties.content:
0:	CHO is introduced in NR to solve robustness/reliability issue.
1:The LTE agreements below are applicable for NR:
a/ CHO is defined as UE having network configuration for initiating access to a target cell based on configured condition(s).
b/ Usage of conditional handover is decided by network. UE evaluates when the condition is valid.
c/ Support configuration of one or more candidate cells for conditional handover;
=>	FFS how many candidate cells (UE and network impacts should be clarified).
=>	FFS how to include the CHO conditions in UE configuration
d/ The baseline operation for Conditional HO procedure assumes HO command type of message contains HO triggering condition(s) and dedicated RRC configuration(s). UE accesses the prepared target when the relevant condition is met.
e/ The baseline operation for Conditional HO assumes the source RAN remains responsible for RRC until UE successfully sends RRC Reconfiguration Complete message to target RAN.
f/ 	RAN2 assumes late packet forwarding (i.e. not done immediately when the CHO target cells become prepared) could be suitable for CHO when there are multiple candidate target cells. Early packet forwarding can also be considered. Detailed decisions require RAN3 study.
2	Cell level quality is used as baseline for CHO execution condition;
FFS: on whether beam quality is used as input for CHO execution condition.
3	 RS type SSB can be used
FFS: CSI-RS, use of more than one RS type
4	Ax events (entry condition) are used for CHO execution condition and A3/5 as baseline
FFS: on other events
5	Trigger quantity for CHO execution condition(RSRP, RSRQ or RS-SINR) is configured by network.
FFS: on multiple quantities.
FFS: Enhancements to the above CHO framework to specifically address usage in FR2 (e.g. address high number of handovers, RLFs, etc)

properties.content:
0:	CHO is introduced in NR to solve robustness/reliability issue.
1:The LTE agreements below are applicable for NR:
a/ CHO is defined as UE having network configuration for initiating access to a target cell based on configured condition(s).
b/ Usage of conditional handover is decided by network. UE evaluates when the condition is valid.
c/ Support configuration of one or more candidate cells for conditional handover;
=>	FFS how many candidate cells (UE and network impacts should be clarified).
=>	FFS how to include the CHO conditions in UE configuration
d/ The baseline operation for Conditional HO procedure assumes HO command type of message contains HO triggering condition(s) and dedicated RRC configuration(s). UE accesses the prepared target when the relevant condition is met.
e/ The baseline operation for Conditional HO assumes the source RAN remains responsible for RRC until UE successfully sends RRC Reconfiguration Complete message to target RAN.
f/ 	RAN2 assumes late packet forwarding (i.e. not done immediately when the CHO target cells become prepared) could be suitable for CHO when there are multiple candidate target cells. Early packet forwarding can also be considered. Detailed decisions require RAN3 study.
2	Cell level quality is used as baseline for CHO execution condition;
FFS: on whether beam quality is used as input for CHO execution condition.
3	 RS type SSB can be used
FFS: CSI-RS, use of more than one RS type
4	Ax events (entry condition) are used for CHO execution condition and A3/5 as baseline
FFS: on other events
5	Trigger quantity for CHO execution condition(RSRP, RSRQ or RS-SINR) is configured by network.
FFS: on multiple quantities.
FFS: Enhancements to the above CHO framework to specifically address usage in FR2 (e.g. address high number of handovers, RLFs, etc)

properties.content:
1: 	Delivering Msg4 and RRC messages in different TBs is allowed and should be supported by all the UEs for the following procedures:
(1) RRC connection establishment;
(2) RRC connection resume;
(3) RRC connection re-establishment.
=>	Companies can double check this working assumption and if there are any concerns then they shall be raised on the RAN2 reflector before the end of the Thursday 18 April 2019. If no concerns are raised then this can be considered agreed, and if concerns are raised then the topic will be discussed again at RAN2#106.
R2-1903676	RRC release with suspend configuration and inter-RAT redirection	MediaTek Inc.	draftCR	Rel-15	38.331	15.5.0	F	NR_newRAT-Core
-	Ericsson think that it is clear in 38.331 that the UE moves to idle when it changes RAT.
-	Intel agree we have this requirement to go to idle. So it would be useless for the network to provide this configuration.
-	ZTE think this can be left to network implementation to avoid this.
-	Huawei think this can be left to network.
-	Qualcomm agree with the intent but nothing is broken as the UE will go to idle immediately. Samsung agree nothing is broken.
-	MediaTek thinks the current requirement for Idle is for IRAT cell reselection but it is not clear if redirection is also consider a reselection.
-	Samsung think that the network could do this and if the UE fails to find an IRAT cell then the UE will stay in inactive.
=>	Revised to make it clear that UE goes to idle for cell selection of an IRAT cell as well as for cell reselection of an IRAT cell. Coversheet and title make also need to be updated

properties.title: RRC release with suspend configuration and inter-RAT redirection

properties.content:
1: 	Delivering Msg4 and RRC messages in different TBs is allowed and should be supported by all the UEs for the following procedures:
(1) RRC connection establishment;
(2) RRC connection resume;
(3) RRC connection re-establishment.
=>	Companies can double check this working assumption and if there are any concerns then they shall be raised on the RAN2 reflector before the end of the Thursday 18 April 2019. If no concerns are raised then this can be considered agreed, and if concerns are raised then the topic will be discussed again at RAN2#106.
R2-1903676	RRC release with suspend configuration and inter-RAT redirection	MediaTek Inc.	draftCR	Rel-15	38.331	15.5.0	F	NR_newRAT-Core
-	Ericsson think that it is clear in 38.331 that the UE moves to idle when it changes RAT.
-	Intel agree we have this requirement to go to idle. So it would be useless for the network to provide this configuration.
-	ZTE think this can be left to network implementation to avoid this.
-	Huawei think this can be left to network.
-	Qualcomm agree with the intent but nothing is broken as the UE will go to idle immediately. Samsung agree nothing is broken.
-	MediaTek thinks the current requirement for Idle is for IRAT cell reselection but it is not clear if redirection is also consider a reselection.
-	Samsung think that the network could do this and if the UE fails to find an IRAT cell then the UE will stay in inactive.
=>	Revised to make it clear that UE goes to idle for cell selection of an IRAT cell as well as for cell reselection of an IRAT cell. Coversheet and title make also need to be updated
=>	Revised in R2-1905370 (Offline discussion 22)
R2-1905370	RRC release with suspend configuration and inter-RAT redirection	MediaTek Inc.	draftCR	Rel-15	38.331	15.5.0	F	NR_newRAT-Core
=>	Agreed in principle
R2-1904545	Note on UE behavior upon T380 expiration	Qualcomm Incorporated	draftCR	Rel-15	38.331	15.5.0	NR_newRAT-Core
=>	Not agreed (already captured in the latest spec by rapporteur CR from last meeting)
R2-1904635	Correction to RRCResumeRequest definition (38.331)	Ericsson	draftCR	Rel-15	38.331	15.5.0	F	NR_newRAT-Core
-	Samsung wonder if we have to specify the size in bits
-	Huawei think the current spec is correct.
=>	Remove the bit sizes from the 2 messages in the rapporteur CR.

properties.Title: Clarification on channel bandwidth capabilities

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: When SRS carrier switching request is used for EN-DC, the report of corresponding capabilities will not be supported.
properties.reasonForChange: Procedures for SRS carrier switching request for EN-DC is currently missing. A generic way to include it, as performed for NR SA case in R2-1902628, is to add the handling of requestedCapabilityNR field to the procedures related to EN-DC capabilities.
properties.summaryOfChange:
5.6.3.3 Reception of the UECapabilityEnquiry by the UE
- Included handling of requestedCapabilityNR for the case EN-DC capabilities were requested

Impact analysis

Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC
 
Impacted functionality: UE Capability transfer
 
Inter-operability: If the network implements the CR and the UE does not, the UE will not report capabilities related to EN-DC SRS carrier switching.
 
If the UE implements the CR and the network does not, the network may expect consistent feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs in UE capability transfer regardless of SRS carrier switching request (i.e. whether srs-SwitchingTimeRequest field is present or not)

-	Samsung understand that according to current spec the UE will release the dedicated config when reconfigurationWithSync with servingCellConfigCommon not including common SUL config is received. And then if SIB1 is later read that included servingCellConfigCommon including common SUL config then the SUL will not be used.
-	ZTE think the alt 5 works and this is as much as we can do for R15.
-	Intel think the current spec is not aligned to previous agreements but also agree that alt 5 can be used but this does cause interruption. The Huawei proposal has capability signalling so it is backwards compatible.
-	Nokia think we have 2 mechanisms that work in Rel-15

-	Qualcomm think that timing alignment might anyway be needed when you change UL. Huawei think there is no issue as a cell with UL and SUL should be time aligned.

=>	RAN2 understanding is that the options supported by existing standards/ implementations for releasing UL configuration are as follows:

•	Reconfiguration including reconfigurationWithSync with servingCellConfigCommon not including common SUL config (Alt5)

properties.title: Update on usage of Need codes

properties.content:
1	For conditions where a field is absent, it is not necessary to include a need code for the following cases:
a)	Parameter clearly is one-shot
b)	Scenario is not supported
c)	No difference whether UE maintains or releases
2	For NZP-CSI-RS-Resource, a change of configuration between periodic, semi-persistent or aperiodic for a NZP-CSI-RS-Resource is not supported without a release and add.
3	For "usage", Reconfiguration between codebook based and non-codebook based transmission is not supported.
4	Add " NOTE 3: UE behaviour on receipt of an RRC message on DCCH or CCCH  that does not include a field that is mandatory  (e.g. because conditions for mandatory presence are fulfilled) is unspecified."
5	Change to betaOffsets are phaseTrackingRS as shown in the document are agreed
6	Add in 6.1.1 " Usage of the text “Network always configures the UE with a value for this field” in the field description indicates that the configuration has to be provided in this or a previous message based on delta configuration.  It does not imply a mandatory presence of the field."
7	Change to periodicityAndOffset as shown in the documents is agreed

properties.Title: Correction on intra-band fallback behavior with FeatureSetsPerCC

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The UE is burdened with a requirement for consistency that conflicts with the requirements for building the FSC list.
properties.reasonForChange:
Currently, TS 38.331 indicates that the UE is required to make the feature set combination IDs in different capability containers consistent with one another:

The UE invokes the procedures in this clause if the NR or E-UTRA network requests UE capabilities for nr, eutra-nr or eutra. This procedure is invoked once per requested rat-Type (see clause 5.6.1.3 for capability enquiry by the NR network; see TS 36.331 [10], clause 5.6.3.3 for capability enquiry by the E-UTRA network). The UE shall ensure that the feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs are consistent across feature sets, feature set combinations and band combinations in all three UE capability containers that the network queries with the same frequencyBandListFilter and with the same eutra-nr-only flag (where applicable).
This requirement is not achievable, as each RAT capability container only includes the FSCs for that RAT, in contrast to the FSs where entries are included if they are referenced by band combinations for other RATs.  The FSC list is built from the supportedBandCombinationList, while the FS list is built from the list of “candidate feature set combinations” based on the list of “candidate band combinations”, meaning that the FS list will contain the needed entries for consistency between containers, but the FSC list will not.

The FSC ID is only referenced within the BandCombination in the supportedBandCombinationList in the same container, so there is no relation between FSCs in different containers.  The requirement for consistency in FSC IDs seems to be spurious.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Remove the feature set combination from the list of IDs that are required to be consistent across containers.
	
Impact analysis

Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone

Impacted functionality:
Capability reporting

Inter-operability:
The CR affects only the UE side; no interoperability problem is possible.

properties.Title: 38.306 Clarification on multiple TA capabilities

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The two timing advances restriction for EN-DC is misleading, and the relationship between multipleTimingAdvances and supportedNumberTAG is unclear. The UE capability reporting might be wrong.
properties.reasonForChange:
The field description of multipleTimingAdvances in CA-ParametersNR in 38306 is extracted as below: 

multipleTimingAdvances(for CA-ParametersNR ) 
Indicates whether multiple timing advances are supported by the UE. For NR CA band combination, if the band combination comprised of more than one band entry (i.e., inter-band or intra-band non-contiguous band combination), the field indicates that different timing advances on different band entries are supported. For EN-DC band combination, this field is not presented and it is mandatory for the UE supporting EN-DC band combination. In this release, up to two timing advances are supported for EN-DC band combination or NR CA band combination.
For NR CA, it is mandatory with IOT bit for inter-band NR CA, otherwise optional. For EN-DC, it is mandatory without IOT bit.

However, it’s very early conclusions on RAN2. After that, RAN1 also discussed similar issues and introduced supportedNumberTAG for NR CA. Then the yellow-highlighted parts conflict with RAN1 introduced capabilities. The yellow-highlighted parts are not needed.

Besides, there are multiple TA capabilities, i.e. multipleTimingAdvance, multipleTimingAdvances and supportedNumberTAG. multipleTimingAdvance is used for LTE side, multipleTimingAdvances and supportedNumberTAG are used for NR side. If the supportedNumberTAG is presented, e.g. indicating n2, n3 or n4, it means UE supports multiple TAs. If the supportedNumberTAG is not presented, it means UE supports single TA. Thus, the multipleTimingAdvances is meaningless.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Dummify the multipleTimingAdvances in TS 38.331 and remove the description of multipleTimingAdvances in TS 38.306.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC and NR SA

Impacted functionality:
UE radio capability

Inter-operability:
1.	   If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability problem, the network will ignore this field, and can acquire the multiple TA capability via supportedNumberTAG.
2.	   If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, the network does not need to decode this field by implementation, and can acquire the multiple TA capability via supportedNumberTAG.

properties.Title: 38.331 Clarification on multiple TA capabilities

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: For for an inter-band ENDC BC with intra-band EN-DC combinations part, if it is required to apply the same UL timing between NR and LTE for intra-band part and UE doesn’t include the capability, an error configuration may happen.
properties.reasonForChange:
In the 15.4.0 version of 38.331, the capability of requiring same UL timing for intra-band EN-DC is introduced in BC level as below:


The definition of ul-TimingAlignmentEUTRA-NR in 38306 is extracted as below: 
  ul-TimingAlignmentEUTRA-NR
Indicates whether to apply the same UL timing between NR and LTE for dynamic power        sharing capable UE operating in intra-band contiguous synchronous EN-DC. If this field is absent, UE should be able to operate with a timing difference up to applicable MTTD requirements when operating in a synchronous intra-band contiguous EN-DC network.
From the definition, it can be seen that this capability is only valid for intra-band EN-DC BC. For an inter-Band EN-DC BC which consists of an intra-band ENDC + inter-(NR or LTE) Band, it is not clear whether this capability could be included.  
A LS R2-1902701 was sent to RAN4 to clarify the issue, and RAN4 disscused this issue in RAN4-90bis and replied to RAN2 in R4-1904879, and clarfied that:
The capability only applies to the intra-band part of the band combination, if the capability is reported for inter-band with intra-band EN-DC combinations.
Therefore, we need to clarify this according to RAN4’s clarification. 
Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC
Impacted functionality:
Capability report for ENDC only
Inter-operability:
 If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE may not indicate this capability(restriction) for an inter-band ENDC BC which has an fallback intra-band ENDC, an error configuration may happen.
 If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there are no inter-operability problems.
properties.summaryOfChange: Clarify that the UE could indicate this capability for an inter-band ENDC with intra-band ENDC part and this capability shall be applied to the intra-band part.

=>	Revised to use the wording from the coversheet " same fields with the same values."

Other filter related documents
R2-1906259	Clarification on the applied freqBandList filter in UE-EUTRA-Capability_option 1	ZTE Corporation, Sanechips	CR	Rel-15	36.331	15.5.1	3977	-	F	NR_newRAT-Core
-	MediaTek this is not needed to have the UE provide the filter back.
-	ZTE think that it is better to have a separate echoed back filter for LTE and NR.
-	Nokia think the only use case is the capability containers are acquired from the UE in different RRC connections.
-	Ericsson think the use case might happen but it is not likely. Intel also agree it is not needed and think it can be avoided without a change.

properties.abstract: Results of Email [106#06][NR] PUCCH reconfiguration on NR UL and SUL (Huawei).
properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The network will need to trigger reconfiguration with sync for moving the PUCCH between the UL and SUL of an SCell, which is unnecessary.
properties.reasonForChange:
In the pucch-Config the field description is unclear on the sentence “The network may also add/remove the pucch-Config in an RRCReconfiguration with reconfigurationWithSync to move the PUCCH between the UL and SUL carrier of one serving. ” as “one serving” is not a complete phrase.

Additionally, RRCReconfiguration with reconfigurationWithSync is an operation that is mostly used by the network to do synchronized configuration for SpCell. For SCells, if such a synchoronized configuration is needed, SCell release and add can be used.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Clarify that, when the network changes the PUCCH configuration between the UL and SUL carrier for a serving cell, reconfigurationWithSync is applicable for SpCell and SCells, but SCell release and add can also be applied for SCell.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone, EN-DC 

Impacted functionality: PUCCH reconfiguration between UL and SUL

Inter-operability:
If the UE implements this change but the network does not, there will be no inter-operability issue as network will never attempt the SCell PUCCH reconfiguration between UL and SUL via Scell release+add.

If the network implements this change, but the UE does not, the network may release and add an SCell to change the PUCCH configuration between the UL and SUL carriers, but the UE does not expect this kind of operation without reconfigurationWithSync, which may cause RRC reconfiguration failure. It is expected UE implementations that support PUCCH on SUL support this CR.

properties.Title: CR to capture UE supported DL/UL bandwidths

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: Handover failure from LTE to NR will possibly happen.
properties.reasonForChange: The condition servCellAdd of initialDownlinkBWP and initialUplinkBWP in the DonlinkConfigCommon and UplinkConfigCommon only describes that the initialDownlinkBWP and initialUplinkBWP are manadatory present upon on serving cell addition (for PSCell and SCell). For handover case from LTE to NR, the initialDownlinkBWP and initialUplinkBWP should be also manadatory present.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Add in the condition servCellAdd of initialDownlinkBWP and initialUplinkBWP that the initialDownlinkBWP and initialUplinkBWP are also manadatory present for hanover from E-UTRA to NR. 


Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: 
Standalone

Impacted functionality: 
Handover from LTE to NR

Inter-operability:
1.	   If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability issue foreseen, as the UE normally performs handover from LTE to NR though the initial BWP of PCell. 
2.	   If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not,  there could be an inter-operability issue. The UE possibly fails to handover to NR from LTE in case that the network does not configure initial BWP of PCell for UE.

properties.Title: Correction on initial BWP configuration in DownlinkConfigCommon and UplinkConfigCommon

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE is unable to report Tx DC location for SUL, which may cause performance degradation for the SUL carrier.
properties.reasonForChange:
When the UE is configured with supplementary uplink carrier, the current RRC signalling does not support UE to report the uplink Tx Direct Current location and 7.5kHz shift for each uplink BWP of both uplink carrier and supplementary uplink carrier for each uplink cell.  UE is only allowed to report these information for one uplink carrier, UL or SUL for each uplink cell.
The current specification does not clearly specify that the reported uplink Tx DC location and 7.5kHz shift per BWP is for the normal uplink carrier or the supplementary uplink carrier or the carrier currently being used when the UE is configured with supplementary uplink carrier and is requested to report uplink Tx Direct Current location. This may lead to the network and the UE may have different understanding about the reported result with current RRC signalling. The DCI-based switching between UL and SUL may also cause discrepancy even if UE reported the TxDC for one of the carriers before the switch.

According to LS R1-1807910, RAN2 agreed that UE should report uplinkTxDirectCurrentList in RRCReconfigurationComplete and RRCResumeComplete message when it receives reportUplinkTxDirectCurrent in RRCReconfiguration message and RRCResume message.
According to newly coming LS R1-1907949, from RAN1’s perspective, UE should, in addition to the normal UL, also report the Tx DC location for supplementary UL when supplementary UL is configured for the UE and the UE is requested to report the Tx DC location.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Extend the existing UL Tx Direct current reporting for each supplementary uplink BWP if UE is configured with supplementary uplink carrier and is requested to report uplink Tx Direct Current location.


Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone, EN-DC

Impacted functionality: Reporting of UL DC location

Inter-operability: 

If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, the network will not comprehend the SUL Tx DC location and will have to determine that by other means, which may cause performance degradation for SUL carrier but no inter-operability problems.
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE will not report SUL Tx DC location even when requested by the network, which may cause performance degradation for SUL carrier but no inter-operability problems.

properties.Title: CR TS 38.306 Clarification on Supported Modulation Order Capability

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: It cannot be guaranteed that UE reported feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs in UE capability transfer are consistent concerning whether srs-SwitchingTimeRequest is present or not in UECapabilityEnquiry.
properties.reasonForChange:
When invoking the procedures in 5.6.1.4 clause, the UE shall ensure that the feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs are consistent across feature sets, feature set combinations and band combinations in all three UE capability containers that the network queries with the same FreqBandList and with the same eutra-nr-only flag (where applicable). 

Hence, it is unclear whether consistency of feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs also applies for SRS carrier switching request. This means that if the network performs a capability request e.g. with a given FreqBandList value and including srs-SwitchingTimeRequest field, when performing a subsequent request with the same FreqBandList value but without including srs-SwitchingTimeRequest field, it may expect that feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs are consistent between former and the subsequent request.

In this manner, it should be clarified that consistency of feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs also applies for SRS carrier switching request. However, to avoid confusion with future filters to be added, a general statement should be included in clause 5.6.1.4 to account that the UE shall ensure that the feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs are consistent for network queries including the same filters with the same values.
properties.summaryOfChange:
5.6.1.4 Settind band combinations, feature set combinations and feature sets supported by the UE
- Clarified that the UE shal ensure that consistent featureSets are reported when UECapabilityEnquiry message includes the same fields with the same values.

Impact analysis

Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone, EN-DC
 
Impacted functionality: UE Capability transfer
 
Inter-operability: If the network implements the CR and the UE does not, there is no inter-operability issue, since the network will expect consistent feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs only if it includes the same values for FreqBandList, eutra-nr-only (if applicable), and SRS carrier switching request (i.e. whether srs-SwitchingTimeRequest field is present or not).
 
If the UE implements the CR and the network does not, the network may expect consistent feature set IDs and feature set combination IDs in UE capability transfer regardless of SRS carrier switching request (i.e. whether srs-SwitchingTimeRequest field is present or not)

properties.Title: TS 36.331 Propagating changes due to TS 38.331 R2-1902709

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: the UE may not indicate the support of LTE SA BC drived form a EN-DC BC, the network needs to reconfigure MCG when SCG is added or removed.
properties.reasonForChange:
In RAN2-adhoc(2018-07), it was agreed that the UE shall support fallback band combinations in LTE SA capability which is derived from MR-DC band combination as below:
Agreements
1	EN-DC UE shall support the LTE standalone band-combination (and all the band combination subsets) derived from a given MR-DC band combination.
This is important for network to keep MCG configuration unchanged when adding or releasing the SCG . However, it is not captured in the current specification.  
In TS 38306, it is stated that the UE shall support the same fallback band combination as below for CA and MR-DC:
A fallback band combination resulting from the reported CA and MR-DC band combination is not signalled but the UE shall support it.
However, the Fallback band combination is defined as the BC with less SCell(s) (not including PSCell) as below:
Fallback band combination: A band combination that would result from another band combination by releasing at least one SCell or uplink configuration of SCell. An intra-band non-contiguous band combination is not considered to be a fallback band combination of an intra-band contiguous band combination.
Therefore, a LTE SA BC is not defined as the fallback BC for a MR-DC BC. We needs to explicitly add the restriction into specification.
Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC

Impacted functionality:
UE radio capability
Inter-operability:
 If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE may not indicate the support of LTE SA BC drived form a EN-DC BC, the network needs to reconfigure MCG when SCG is added or removed.
 If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there are no inter-operability problems.
properties.summaryOfChange: Capture the agreement into the spec.

properties.summaryOfChange:
Remove “and feature sets” in the procedure text for the case of ue-CapabilityRequest including eutra-nr is requested. 

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options:
EN-DC

Impacted functionality:
Removing a requirement to include feature sets in MRDC container for UE capability information (i.e. it is not possible to include featuresets in MRDC container)

Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no problem because there are no ways to include feature sets in MRDC container based on the description and ASN.1 for TS 38.331..
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no problem because featuresets are not included in the MRDC container for UE capability information in this case.

properties.Title: Correction on description of additionalActiveSpatialRelationPUCCH

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE can only perform handover using a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell, in other cases related to reconfiguration with sync, e.g. PSCell addition, it can not support to use a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell.
properties.reasonForChange:
In the definition for the Phy-Parameter csi-RS-CFRA-ForHO in 4.2.7.10 in TS 38.306, it is specified that this field “indicates whether the UE can perform handover using a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell.” 
Actually it is a UE capability of performing a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell, it can be applied in many cases related to reconfiguration with sync, such as PSCell addition, in addition to only handover.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Clarify the definition of csi-RS-CFRA-ForHO that it indicates whether the UE can perform reconfiguration with sync using a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell. 


Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: 
Standalone, EN-DC 

Impacted functionality: 
UE capability for RACH

Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the network may configure UE to perform PSCell addition using a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell, in this case UE behaviour is not specified and it may lead to a reconfiguration failure.
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue, since the network may still configure UE to perform handover using a contention free random access on PRACH resources that are associated with CSI-RS resources of the target cell.

properties.Title: Corrections to UE Capability definitions

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The two timing advances restriction for EN-DC is misleading, and the relationship between multipleTimingAdvances and supportedNumberTAG is unclear. The UE capability reporting might be wrong.
properties.reasonForChange:
The field description of multipleTimingAdvances in CA-ParametersNR in 38306 is extracted as below: 

multipleTimingAdvances(for CA-ParametersNR ) 
Indicates whether multiple timing advances are supported by the UE. For NR CA band combination, if the band combination comprised of more than one band entry (i.e., inter-band or intra-band non-contiguous band combination), the field indicates that different timing advances on different band entries are supported. For EN-DC band combination, this field is not presented and it is mandatory for the UE supporting EN-DC band combination. In this release, up to two timing advances are supported for EN-DC band combination or NR CA band combination.
For NR CA, it is mandatory with IOT bit for inter-band NR CA, otherwise optional. For EN-DC, it is mandatory without IOT bit.

However, it’s very early conclusions on RAN2. After that, RAN1 also discussed similar issues and introduced supportedNumberTAG for NR CA. Then the yellow-highlighted parts conflict with RAN1 introduced capabilities. The yellow-highlighted parts are not needed.

Besides, there are multiple TA capabilities, i.e. multipleTimingAdvance, multipleTimingAdvances and supportedNumberTAG. multipleTimingAdvance is used for LTE side, multipleTimingAdvances and supportedNumberTAG are used for NR side. If the supportedNumberTAG is presented, e.g. indicating n2, n3 or n4, it means UE supports multiple TAs. If the supportedNumberTAG is not presented, it means UE supports single TA. Thus, the multipleTimingAdvances is meaningless.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Dummify the multipleTimingAdvances in TS 38.331 and remove the description of multipleTimingAdvances in TS 38.306.

Add the description to clarify that in NR CA if the band combination comprised of more than one band entry (i.e., inter-band or intra-band non-contiguous band combination), it indicates that different timing advances on different band entries are supported.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC and NR SA

Impacted functionality:
UE radio capability

Inter-operability:
1.	   If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability problem, the network will ignore this field, and can acquire the multiple TA capability via supportedNumberTAG.
2.	   If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, the network does not need to decode this field by implementation, and can acquire the multiple TA capability via supportedNumberTAG.

properties.Title: Clarification on pdsch-ProcessingType2

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP may not always be presented by the UE, the network may be confused about the capability of TCI states.
properties.reasonForChange:
The field multipleTCI shall be always set to 1, which means UE always supports more than one TCI state configurations per CORESET. And we can infer that UE always supports more than one TCI state configurations for PDSCH. 

Thus, for tci-StatePDSCH, the maxNumberConfiguredTCIstatesPerCC should always be presented and at least n4 is indicated; regarding maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP, at least one active TCI state should supported, the maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP should always be presented and at least n1 is indicated. Although we can define that one active TCI state is supported if maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP is absent, it would lead to understanding confusion for the network side. So a clearer way is that maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP is always present.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Add the description that maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP shall always be present.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC and NR SA

Impacted functionality:
UE radio capability

Inter-operability:
1.	   If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE may not report maxNumberActiveTCI-PerBWP if implements incorrectly, which leads to confusion in network side.
2.	   If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no inter-operability problem, the UE reports the capability correctly and the network can understand them according to the field description.

properties.abstract: Results of Email [106#09][NR]: Need codes CR (Intel).
properties.consequencesIfNotApproved:
Ambigous specifications can lead to inter-operability issues.

Impact analysis:
Impacted architecture: EN-DC, SA
Impacted functionality: 
CSI-AperiodicTriggerStateList, NZP-CSI-RS-Resource, tpc-PUCCH, PUCCH/PUCCHless Scell reconfiguration, codebook and non-codebook tx reconfiguration.                           

If network is not implemented according to this CR and UE is, network may provide reconfigurations that are not supported resulting in failure of reconfiguration and possibility re-establishment.
If UE is not implemented according to this CR and network is, there is no inter-operability issue.
properties.reasonForChange:
Update of the specifications on usage of Need codes in conditions as per agreements in R2-105bis.
Usage of Need codes is currently ambigous in a number of places, especially in conditions.
Error handling on missing mandatorily present fields in conditions in DCCH, CCCH messages is incorrect and not aligned with the agreement in R2-105bis.
Usage of "Field is always configured by the network…" in the field description when the fields is not necessarily present in the condition (due to use of Need M) is confusing.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Usage of text "Network always configures the UE with a value for this field" clarified with a NOTE.
Rules and guidance for usage of Need node in conditions for "absent" introduced.
Network restrictions imposed in several cases where there was an ambiguity in UE behaviour during reconfigurations:
a)	Reconfiguration of CSI-AssociatedReportConfigInfo is not supported
b)	A change of configuration between periodic, semi-persistent or aperiodic for a NZP-CSI-RS-Resource is not supported without a release and add
c)	Reconfiguration between a PUCCH and PUCCHless Scell is only supported using an Scell release and add.
d)	Reconfiguration between codebook based and non-codebook based transmission is not supported.
e)	Reconfiguration of a ZP-CSI-RS-Resource between periodic or semi-persistent and aperiodic is not supported.
f)	Network always configures the UE with a value for periodicityAndOffset for periodic and semi-persistent ZP-CSI-RS resource (as indicated in PDSCH-Config)
Failure handling in UE for missing conditional mandatory fields changed to make the UE behaviour unspecified.
Editorial change to replace "not present" with "absent" for consistency.
Included changes from R2-1904657, R2-1904656 and R2-1905409.
properties.title: Update on usage of Need codes

properties.content:
1	For conditions where a field is absent, it is not necessary to include a need code for the following cases:
a)	Parameter clearly is one-shot
b)	Scenario is not supported
c)	No difference whether UE maintains or releases
2	For NZP-CSI-RS-Resource, a change of configuration between periodic, semi-persistent or aperiodic for a NZP-CSI-RS-Resource is not supported without a release and add.
3	For "usage", Reconfiguration between codebook based and non-codebook based transmission is not supported.
4	Add " NOTE 3: UE behaviour on receipt of an RRC message on DCCH or CCCH  that does not include a field that is mandatory  (e.g. because conditions for mandatory presence are fulfilled) is unspecified."
5	Change to betaOffsets are phaseTrackingRS as shown in the document are agreed
6	Add in 6.1.1 " Usage of the text “Network always configures the UE with a value for this field” in the field description indicates that the configuration has to be provided in this or a previous message based on delta configuration.  It does not imply a mandatory presence of the field."
7	Change to periodicityAndOffset as shown in the documents is agreed

properties.Title: Clarification on supported modulation order capability
properties.Source: Nokia, Nokia Shanghai Bell, Huawei, HiSilicon, Ericsson

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The UE may not indicate the two IEs together, in that case, the network could not handle the non-codebook based PUSCH capability correctly.
properties.reasonForChange:
In the RAN1 feature list, the non-codebook based PUSCH transmission inlcudes three parts and they are needed to be reported together:
1. Maximal number of supported layers (non-codebook transmission scheme)
2. Supported max number of SRS resource per set (SRS set use is configured as for non-codebook transmission).
3. Maximum number of simultaneous transmitted SRS resources at one symbol
However, in TS 38.331, the three parts are grouped into two IEs (maxNumberMIMO-LayersNonCB, mimo-NonCB-PUSCH):




In TS 38.306, the three parts are defined as three separate capabilities:
maxNumberMIMO-LayersCB-PUSCH
maxNumberMIMO-LayersNonCB-PUSCH
maxNumberMIMO-LayersNonCB-PUSCH

However, there currently is no explicit restriction to require the UE to report these three IEs together.
In addition, there are some references to “non-codebook based PUSCH transmission” in TS 38.306 but it is not so clear on the exact definition of non-codebook based PUSCH transmission.
Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC and NR SA
Impacted functionality:
UE radio capability
Inter-operability:
  If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, the UE may not indicate the two IEs together, this may would casue that the the non-codebook based PUSCH transmission can’t be used.
  If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there are no inter-operability problems.
properties.summaryOfChange: Clarify that non-codebook based PUSCH transmission includes maxNumberMIMO-LayersNonCB, mimo-NonCB-PUSCH and the UE should report maxNumberMIMO-LayersNonCB, mimo-NonCB-PUSCH together.

properties.summaryOfChange:
Clarify that the UE shall support the number of PRBs of CORESET#0 as defined in TS 38.213 for both the downlink and the uplink.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options:
EN-DC, Standalone

Impacted functionality:
BWP

Inter-operability:
If the UE is implemented according to this CR but the network is not, the network does not know how many PRBs the UE can support for the initial BWP and may configure bandwidth of the initial BWP to the number of PRBs which is not supported by the UE. As a consequence, the UE may not be able to camp on this cell.
If the network is implemented according to this CR, but the UE is not, the network may assume the UE supporting the number of PRBs of CORESET#0 for both downlink and uplink, but the UE may not support. As a consequence, the UE may not be able to camp on this cell.

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: Some UEs may interpretate the number of DRBs that a UE shall support could be more than 16 in case of some DRBs are configured with duplication.
properties.reasonForChange:
From the current specification, UE should at least support 8 DRBs per MAC entity if any DRB is configured with duplicaiton, i.e. “8 per MAC entity with duplication.”
However, the statement “16 without duplication” only implies UE should at least support total 16 DRBs per UE in case of no duplicaiton. When some DRBs are configured with duplicaiton and some DRBs are not, it is not clear whether more than 16 DRBs should be supported by the UE.
Therefore, the intented UE capability is, regardless with or without duplicaiton, the maximum number of DRBs to support is 16 (all cases).
properties.summaryOfChange:
Clarify the value of #DRBs is “16 per UE”;
Change “8 per MAC entity with duplication.” into a NOTE.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: EN-DC
Impacted functionality:
Number of DRB

Inter-operability: 
If the UE is implemented according to this CR but the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue foreseen, because the intented UE capabliity has not been changed.

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: The UE cannot include additional FeatureSetsDownlink with fewer carriers (by including fewer FSDpCC) but with additional functionality. Hence, it has to advertise additional band combinations with additional FeatureSetCombinations and lower BWCs which introduces additional signalling overhead and defeats the purpose of the FeatureSet / FeatureSetPerCC structure.
properties.reasonForChange:
As a result of long discussions in RAN2 the concept of feature-sets and feature-sets-per-CC was introduced with the intention to reduce signalling overhead by minimizing the number of explicitly signalled fallback band combinations and by re-using FSs, FSpCCs and FSCs across band combinations. RAN2 discussed how a UE could advertise additional functionality when configured with a subset of the serving cells and captured the following in section 6.3.3 - FeatureSetCombination: 

NOTE 1:	The UE may advertise fallback band-combinations in which it supports additional functionality explicitly in two ways: Either by setting FeatureSet IDs to zero (inter-band and intra-band non-contiguous fallback) and by reducing the number of FeatureSet-PerCC Ids in a Feature Set (intra-band contiguous fallback). Or by separate BandCombination entries with associated FeatureSetCombinations.
Since it became clear that RAN4 would still require configuration of bandwidth classes, RAN2 explained in the same section that the number of supported serving cells is determined by the minimum of what the BWC allows and by the number of FSpCC entries: 

The FeatureSetUplink and FeatureSetDownlink referred to from the FeatureSet comprise, among other information, a set of FeatureSetUplinkPerCC-Id:s and FeatureSetDownlinkPerCC-Id:s. The number of these per-CC IDs determines the number of carriers that the UE is able to aggregate contiguously in frequency domain in the corresponding band. The number of carriers supported by the UE is also restricted by the supportedBandwidthCombinationSet indicated in the associated BandCombination, if present.
This text allows the UE to define FeatureSets with different numbers and different types of FeatureSetsPerCC and to list them all in a single FeatureSetCombination referred to from a single Band Combination. For example, the UE could add …
1) an FSD with 4 FSDpCCs that support 2L-MIMO and 64QAM, and
2) an FSD with 3 FSDpCCs that support 2L-MIMO and 256QAM, and 
3) an FSD with 2 FSDpCCs that support 4L-MIMO and 256QAM

All this information would be comprised in a single band combination which would also indicate one BWC value for e.g. up to 4CCs. The NW deduces that it may configure up to 4 serving cells with 2L+64QAM or 3 serving cells with 2L-MIMO and 256QAM or 2 serving cells with 4L-MIMO and 256 QAM.

However, at a later point in time an unnecessary restriction was introduced in the field descriptions of featureSetListPerDownlinkCC and featureSetListPerUplinkCC, which seems to forbid what the section above allows and encourages: "The UE shall hence include as many FeatureSetDownlinkPerCC-Id in this list as the number of carriers it supports according to the ca-BandwidthClassDL". Due to this constraint the UE was not allowed to include more or fewer FSpCCs than the BWC in the band combination supports. To provide the same information as exemplified above, a UE would have to include 3 separate band combinations with 3 separate FSCs pointing to different FSs containing different FSpCCs. 

In version v15.5.0 the term "at least" was added, which again allowed the UE to include FeatureSetsDownlink for more carriers (more FSD/UpCC). This addition was functionally OK even though of somewhat questionable benefit… at least it would not help for the case exemplified above. When seeing it in isolation, the change was non-backwards compatible from network perspective since a network following strictly the field descriptions of featureSetListPerDownlinkCC and featureSetListPerUplinkCC might not be able to handle FSs with more FSpCCs. However, since the text in the IE section of the FeatureSetCombination allowed that case, it was OK to assume that networks could handle that case, too. 

Unfortunately, the main issue persists, i.e., the field description in v15.5.0 is still in contradiction with the description in the IE section and it would prevent UEs from listing explicit fallback band combinations with additional functionality on fewer CCs unless they signal additional Band Combinations. 

Concerns were raised that this would be a NBC change. It is however worth pointing out that, like the change done in 15.5.0, it is primarily removing an ambiguity between two sections and that it is only a change to the network but not to the UE.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Remove the unncessary restrictions in the field descriptions of featureSetListPerDownlinkCC and featureSetListPerUplinkCC which requires the the UE to include at least as many FSpCC as it supports in accordance to its BWC and which thereby contradicts the description in the IE section of the FeatureSetCombination. 

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone, EN-DC

Impacted functionality: UE Capability signalling

Inter-operability: 
The CR resolves a contradiction, which was introduced in 15.5.0, in the indication of intra-band contiguous fallback capability. Therefore, there can be no confidence that different implementations will inter-operate with each other. As a consequence it is critical that all implementations are aligned with this CR.

If the UE is implemented according to the CR but the NW is not (i.e., the NW strictly follows the field description of featureSetListPerDownlinkCC and featureSetListPerUplinkCC), the NW may expect the FeatureSet to contain at least as many FSpCCs as the BWC in the associated BC indicates. Such network may consider the FeatureSet as not suitable for its intended configuration and it would instead use another FeatureSet containing as many or more FSpCC as the BWC suggestes. Hence, the NW will still be able to configure the UE but it would not be able to utilize the additional functionality that the UE advertised in the additional FeatureSet. 

If the NW is implemented according to the CR but the UE is not not (i.e., the UE strictly follows the field description of featureSetListPerDownlinkCC and featureSetListPerUplinkCC), there is no interoperability issue since the UE will not advertise FeatureSets with fewer FSpCCs than the BWC suggests.

properties.Title: TS 36.331 Propagating changes due to TS 38.331 R2-1902709

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE has to support additionalActiveSpatialRelationPUCCH even when maxNumberActiveSpatialRelations is set to larger than 1, which is in fact duplicated capability information and just leads to unnecessary signalling overhead.
properties.reasonForChange:
The current spec in TS 38.306 has incorrectly captured the parameter description of additionalActiveSpatialRelationPUCCH as “It is applicable if maxNumberActiveSpatialRelations is supported”. 
According to the attachment in RAN1 LS (R1-1905868) as shown in the figure below, FG 2-61 is only applicable on condition that FG 2-60 is set to 1. That is to say, the additionalActiveSpatialRelationPUCCH is applicable only if maxNumberActiveSpatialRelations is set to 1 rather than supported.

And in current TS 38.306, it is still not so clear what the meaning is when it refers to ‘it is mandatory’, so it needs to clarify that if it is to say ‘it is mandatory to report’ or ‘it is mandatory with capability signalling’.
properties.summaryOfChange:
Clarify that additionalActiveSpatialRelationPUCCH is mandatory with capability signalling if maxNumberActiveSpatialRelations is set to 1.  
Change ‘it is mandatory’ to ‘it is mandatory to report’ or ‘it is mandatory with capability signalling’ case by case

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: 
Standalone, EN-DC 


Impacted functionality:
UE capability on the number of active spatial relation for PUCCH.

Inter-operability:
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability issue. The UE supporting more than 1 active spatial relation for uplink will report supporting addtional active spatial relation for PUCCH, it will not lead to reconfiguration failure even if the network enables this additional spatial relation.
If the UE is implemented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue, since the network will configure UE based on derived UE capability report, it will not exceed the scope of UE capability.

properties.Title: Correction on intra-band fallback behavior with FeatureSetsPerCC

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE capability of maxUplinkDutyCycle for FR2 is not  supported and UE may need to scale down the power density for UL transmissions to be in compliance with electromagnetic power density exposure requirements.
properties.reasonForChange:
In RAN4#90 meeting in February, RAN4 agreed the LS on FR2 maxUplinkDutyCycle capability values (R4-1902489) and sent the LS to inform RAN2 on the signalling impact. The content of LS is provided as below:

In RAN #83 meeting in March, the issue of minimum value 2% was raised and the FR2 maximum UL duty cycle was discussed in RAN plenary meeting. According to the agreed way forward (RP-190755)

In RAN2#106 meeting, RAN2 received LS from RAN4 on FR2 maxUplinkDutyCycle (R2-1908432 )
properties.summaryOfChange:
A UE capability of maxUplinkDutyCycle-FR2 is introduced to indicate the maximum percentage of symbols during 1s that can be scheduled for uplink transmission without UE power reduction to ensure UE compliance with applicable electromagnetic power density exposure requirements provided by regulatory bodies.

Impact analysis
Impacted functionality: UL scheduling

Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone, EN-DC

Inter-operability: 
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability issue as UE will not indicate the capability so the network will schedule the UE according to the absence of the capability.
If the UE is implenented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue as the network will not consider the UE capability so the network may schedule with more UL than indicated by the duty cycle, in which case the UE behaves according to 38.101-2.

properties.Title: CR on capability of maxUplinkDutyCycle for FR2

properties.consequencesIfNotApproved: UE capability of maxUplinkDutyCycle for FR2 is not supported and UE may need to scale down the power density for UL transmissions to be in compliance with electromagnetic power density exposure requirements
properties.reasonForChange:
In RAN4#90 meeting in February, RAN4 agreed the LS on FR2 maxUplinkDutyCycle capability values R4-1902489 and sent the LS to inform RAN2 on the signalling impact. The content of LS is provided as below:

In RAN #83 meeting in March, the issue of minimum value 2% was raised and the FR2 maximum UL duty cycle was discussed in RAN plenary meeting. According to the agreed way forward (RP-190755)

In RAN2#106 meeting, RAN2 received LS from RAN4 on FR2 maxUplinkDutyCycle (R2-1908432 )
properties.summaryOfChange:
A UE capability of maxUplinkDutyCycle-FR2 is introduced to indicate the maximum percentage of symbols during 1s that can be scheduled for uplink transmission without UE power reduction to ensure UE compliance with applicable electromagnetic power density exposure requirements provided by regulatory bodies.

Impact analysis
Impacted 5G architecture options: Standalone, EN-DC

Impacted functionality: UL scheduling (for FR2)

Inter-operability: 
If the network is implemented according to the CR and the UE is not, there is no inter-operability issue as UE will not indicate the capability so the network will schedule the UE according to the absence of the capability.
If the UE is implenented according to the CR and the network is not, there is no inter-operability issue as the network will not consider the UE capability so the network may schedule with more UL than indicated by the duty cycle, in which case the UE behaves according to 38.101-2
